UN.name: United Nations
UN.text: The world's main international organisation, where almost every country has a seat and a vote.

EU.name: European Union
EU.text: A union of European countries that share a single market, many common laws and, for most, the euro.

NATO.name: NATO
NATO.text: A military alliance of countries in Europe and North America that promise to defend each other.

AU.name: African Union
AU.text: An organisation of the countries of Africa that works on peace, trade and development across the continent.

ASEAN.name: ASEAN
ASEAN.text: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations, which works on trade and cooperation in South-East Asia.

COMMONWEALTH.name: Commonwealth of Nations
COMMONWEALTH.text: A group of countries, most of them once part of the British Empire, that work together on shared goals.

OPEC.name: OPEC
OPEC.text: The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, a group of oil producers that coordinate how much oil they pump.

ARAB_LEAGUE.name: Arab League
ARAB_LEAGUE.text: An organisation of Arab countries in the Middle East and Africa.

GCC.name: Gulf Cooperation Council
GCC.text: A political and economic union of six Arab countries on the Persian Gulf.

G20.name: G20
G20.text: A group of the world's biggest economies whose leaders meet every year. The EU and the African Union are also members.

BRICS.name: BRICS
BRICS.text: A group of large emerging economies, named after its first members: Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa.

MERCOSUR.name: Mercosur
MERCOSUR.text: A South American trade bloc whose members trade with each other without most customs duties.

CARICOM.name: CARICOM
CARICOM.text: The Caribbean Community, which links Caribbean countries through trade and cooperation.

PIF.name: Pacific Islands Forum
PIF.text: The main organisation of countries in the Pacific Ocean, which works on issues such as climate change and fishing.
